shortDescription: Latvian airline airBaltic is preparing workforce layoffs that could affect about 500 to 700 positions across its bases in Riga, Vilnius and Tallinn.($1 = 0.8922 euros)

children: Latvian airline airBaltic is preparing workforce layoffs that could affect about 500 to 700 positions across its bases in Riga, Vilnius and Tallinn.
The carrier filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New York in September, aiming to complete a sweeping restructuring focused on cutting its mounting debt through capacity and fleet reductions
AirBaltic gained approval last month to access €140 million ($157 million) from a wider €350 million financing package
CEO Erno Hilden told Reuters in September that the airline was in talks with labour unions over "an adjustment" to the workforce
The company said on Monday that it is in talks with unions on potential reduced workload arrangements for pilots and cabin crew
New organisational structures for the rest of the company are expected to be defined by mid-October, airBaltic said
The final number of layoffs could change within the course of the process, it added
